requirements.title: Code mode tool construction and reachability validation
requirements.rationale: Validating tool names and preventing recursive code mode nesting at construction ensures safe reachability declarations and prevents infinite execution recursion.

criteria.condition: codemode.New is called with a slice of tools and codemode.Options
criteria.action: construct a core.Tool whose Name matches opts.Name (defaulting to 'code_mode'), ReachableTools matches the input tools, and Execute dispatches to the script runner
criteria.contract: tool.Name matches opts.Name (defaulting to 'code_mode' if empty); tool.ReachableTools matches the supplied tools slice; tool.Execute dispatches execution to the script runner

setup: a slice of core.Tool instances and codemode.Options with custom Name
check.pseudocode:
t, _, err := codemode.New([]core.Tool{dummyTool}, codemode.Options{Name: "custom_mode"})
assert err == nil
assert t.Name == "custom_mode"
assert len(t.ReachableTools) == 1
assert t.Execute != nil

criteria.action: define InputSchema requiring a string property 'script' and OutputSchema specifying output string, return_value any, and calls_completed array
criteria.contract: InputSchema requires a string property 'script' with execution description; OutputSchema specifies output string, return_value any, and calls_completed array

setup: a valid tool slice
check.pseudocode:
t, _, err := codemode.New(tools, codemode.Options{})
assert err == nil
assert t.InputSchema != nil
assert t.InputSchema.Properties["script"].Type == "string"
assert t.InputSchema.IsRequired("script")
assert t.OutputSchema != nil
assert t.OutputSchema.Properties["output"].Type == "string"
assert t.OutputSchema.Properties["calls_completed"].Type == "array"

criteria.condition: codemode.New is called where any tool in tools matches opts.Name or is an existing code-mode tool
criteria.action: reject construction and return an error preventing code-mode self-nesting
criteria.contract: returns an error containing 'codemode: cannot bind code_mode tool inside code_mode'

setup: a tool slice containing a tool named 'code_mode' or an existing code-mode tool instance
check.pseudocode:
_, _, err := codemode.New([]core.Tool{{Name: "code_mode"}}, codemode.Options{Name: "code_mode"})
assert err != nil
assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "codemode: cannot bind code_mode tool inside code_mode")

criteria.condition: codemode.New is called with duplicate tool names in the tools slice
criteria.action: reject construction and return an error naming the duplicated tool name
criteria.contract: returns an error containing 'codemode: duplicate tool name: <name>'

setup: a tool slice containing two tools with identical names
check.pseudocode:
tools := []core.Tool{{Name: "lookup"}, {Name: "lookup"}}
_, _, err := codemode.New(tools, codemode.Options{})
assert err != nil
assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "codemode: duplicate tool name: lookup")

criteria.condition: opts.Guidelines is provided in Options
criteria.action: assign the custom guidelines to core.Tool.PromptGuidelines, or populate default code-mode guidance when omitted
criteria.contract: the custom guidelines slice is assigned to tool.PromptGuidelines when provided; default code-mode guidance is populated when Guidelines is omitted

setup: options configured with custom PromptGuidelines, and options omitting Guidelines
check.pseudocode:
t1, _, _ := codemode.New(tools, codemode.Options{Guidelines: []string{"custom guide"}})
assert len(t1.PromptGuidelines) == 1 && t1.PromptGuidelines[0] == "custom guide"
t2, _, _ := codemode.New(tools, codemode.Options{})
assert len(t2.PromptGuidelines) > 0

criteria.action: for any valid tool slice and options passed to codemode.New, return a BuildInfo reporting DescriptionBytes, DescriptionChars, and BoundToolsCount matching the bound tools count and description text
criteria.contract: BuildInfo.BoundToolsCount equals len(tools); BuildInfo.DescriptionBytes equals len([]byte(tool.Description)); BuildInfo.DescriptionChars equals utf8.RuneCountInString(tool.Description)

setup: a generator of arbitrary valid core.Tool slices and options
check.pseudocode:
for tools, opts in gen_valid_tools_and_opts():
    t, info, err := codemode.New(tools, opts)
    assert err == nil
    assert info.BoundToolsCount == len(tools)
    assert info.DescriptionBytes == len([]byte(t.Description))
    assert info.DescriptionChars == utf8.RuneCountInString(t.Description)

requirements.title: Dynamic description and typed schema generation
requirements.rationale: Generating dynamic Starlark signatures from tool input and output schemas informs the model of available functions and parameter types without manual documentation drift.

criteria.condition: codemode.New constructs a tool description and opts.Description is not empty
criteria.action: use opts.Description directly as the tool description without dynamic rendering
criteria.contract: tool.Description equals opts.Description exactly; dynamic template rendering is bypassed

setup: options specifying an explicit Description string override
check.pseudocode:
desc := "Explicit override description"
t, _, err := codemode.New(tools, codemode.Options{Description: desc})
assert err == nil
assert t.Description == desc

criteria.condition: codemode.New constructs a tool description and opts.Description is empty
criteria.action: render the description by combining the runtime instructions template with typed Starlark function signatures derived from bound tools
criteria.contract: description documents runtime constraints including keyword-only arguments, error return conventions, parallel execution, and no ambient I/O; description includes typed Starlark function signatures for each bound tool

setup: options with empty Description and a list of bound tools
check.pseudocode:
t, _, err := codemode.New([]core.Tool{toolA, toolB}, codemode.Options{})
assert err == nil
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, "Starlark")
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, "keyword arguments")
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, "parallel")
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, "is_error")
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, toolA.Name)
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, toolB.Name)

criteria.condition: opts.DescriptionTemplate is configured in Options
criteria.action: render the instructions section using the caller-supplied Go text/template string in place of the default template
criteria.contract: the rendered instructions section uses the custom template output in place of the default

setup: options specifying a custom DescriptionTemplate string
check.pseudocode:
tmpl := "Custom header: {{.ToolCount}} tools."
t, _, err := codemode.New([]core.Tool{toolA}, codemode.Options{DescriptionTemplate: tmpl})
assert err == nil
assert strings.Contains(t.Description, "Custom header: 1 tools.")

criteria.action: for any bound tool with an InputSchema, generate a Starlark signature mapping JSON Schema property types to str, int, float, bool, list, or dict, marking optional fields with '= None'
criteria.contract: property types map to str, int, float, bool, list, or dict respectively; optional properties are marked with default '= None'

setup: a generator of tool schemas containing diverse property types and required flags

criteria.condition: the schema generator inspects a bound tool with a non-nil OutputSchema
criteria.action: render the documented return type using the OutputSchema field names and types, defaulting to 'Any' when OutputSchema is nil
criteria.contract: tool with non-nil OutputSchema renders documented return type using OutputSchema field names and types; tool with nil OutputSchema documents return type as 'Any'

setup: a tool with structured OutputSchema and a tool with nil OutputSchema
check.pseudocode:
sig1 := codemode.RenderSignature(toolWithOutputSchema)
assert strings.Contains(sig1, "status: str")
sig2 := codemode.RenderSignature(toolWithoutOutputSchema)
assert strings.Contains(sig2, "Any")

criteria.action: document runtime constraints in the instructions section including keyword-only arguments, error return conventions, parallel execution, and lack of ambient I/O

requirements.title: Sandboxed Starlark runtime isolation
requirements.rationale: Restricting Starlark globals and module loaders ensures model scripts cannot access the host filesystem, network, environment variables, or execution clock.

criteria.condition: a code-mode script invocation begins execution
criteria.action: create an isolated starlark.Thread populated with safe language builtins, bound tool callables, and helpers parallel, call, and is_error
criteria.contract: starlark.Thread globals contain safe builtins (len, range, print, type, etc.); globals include bound tool callables, parallel, call, and is_error

setup: a script executing in code mode

criteria.condition: a script attempts to execute a load statement
criteria.action: refuse dynamic module loading and fail the thread
criteria.contract: returns an error stating 'load is not permitted in code_mode scripts'

setup: a script containing a 'load(...)' module import statement
check.pseudocode:
res := runScript(ctx, "load('math.star', 'pi')")
assert !res.OK
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "load is not permitted in code_mode scripts")

criteria.action: for any script execution, omit all host system primitives including open, os, socket, http, os.environ, subprocesses, and time functions from module globals
criteria.contract: attempting to access any host primitive fails with an undefined identifier error; no ambient host I/O primitives exist in module globals

setup: a generator of host primitive names (open, os, socket, http, environ, subprocess, time)
check.pseudocode:
for name in ["open", "os", "socket", "http", "environ", "subprocess", "time"]:
    res := runScript(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("val = %s", name))
    assert !res.OK
    assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "undefined")

requirements.title: Keyword-argument tool bindings and invocation
requirements.rationale: Binding tools as keyword-only functions guarantees parameter mapping fidelity to underlying JSON schemas while preventing argument position misalignment.

criteria.condition: a script invokes a bound tool function with one or more positional arguments
criteria.action: reject the call and halt the function execution with a Starlark error
criteria.contract: returns a Starlark error containing '<tool> only accepts keyword arguments'

setup: a bound tool 'fetch' registered in code mode
check.pseudocode:
res := runScript(ctx, "fetch('http://example.com')")
assert !res.OK
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "fetch only accepts keyword arguments")

criteria.condition: a bound tool is invoked with keyword arguments
criteria.action: convert Starlark argument values into Go JSON-compatible structures and dispatch a core.ToolUseBlock via core.CallNested
criteria.contract: Starlark keyword arguments are converted into Go JSON-compatible structures and dispatched via core.CallNested; structured Data map is converted into Starlark dicts and returned to the script

setup: a bound tool registered and a mock nested dispatcher returning structured Data

criteria.condition: a nested tool call dispatched via core.CallNested succeeds with OK set to true and ToolResult.Data is non-nil
criteria.action: convert the structured Data map into Starlark dicts, lists, and primitives and return the converted value to the script

criteria.condition: a nested tool call dispatched via core.CallNested succeeds with OK set to true and ToolResult.Data is nil
criteria.action: return a Starlark dictionary containing {'text': ToolResult.Text} to the script
criteria.contract: the call returns a Starlark dictionary containing {'text': 'done'}; script accesses res['text'] without error

setup: a bound tool returning OK=true, Text='done', and nil Data

criteria.condition: a nested tool call dispatched via core.CallNested returns core.ErrTerminated
criteria.action: immediately halt script execution and propagate Terminate set to true on the code-mode ToolResult
criteria.contract: code_mode tool execution stops and ToolResult.Terminate is true

setup: a bound tool whose execution returns core.ErrTerminated from CallNested

criteria.condition: a nested tool call dispatched via core.CallNested is aborted by context cancellation
criteria.action: halt script execution and return an abortion failure result
criteria.contract: returns core.ToolResult with OK: false and Error: 'aborted'

setup: a cancellable context and a bound tool invoked during cancellation
check.pseudocode:
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
dispatcher.OnCall = func(b core.ToolUseBlock) (core.ToolResult, error) {
    cancel()
    return core.ToolResult{}, context.Canceled
}
res := runScript(ctx, "slow_op()")
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "aborted"

requirements.title: Non-exceptional tool error values
requirements.rationale: Exposing tool errors as structured values rather than raising Starlark exceptions allows scripts to inspect error states and apply fallback logic without halting execution.

criteria.condition: a nested tool call dispatched via core.CallNested returns a ToolResult and ToolResult.OK is false
criteria.action: construct and return a ToolError Starlark value without raising a runtime exception
criteria.contract: function returns a ToolError Starlark value; no runtime exception is raised and script execution continues

setup: a bound tool returning ToolResult{OK: false, Error: 'not_found', Detail: 'item missing'}

criteria.action: for any ToolError value, set type(val) to 'tool_error', set attributes ok to False, is_error to True, error to the error code string, detail to the detail string, and data to the error payload
criteria.contract: type(val) is 'tool_error'; attributes ok is False and is_error is True; error matches error code, detail matches detail string, data matches payload

setup: a generator of failing ToolResult instances with varied Error, Detail, and Data payloads
check.pseudocode:
for tr in gen_failing_tool_results():
    te := codemode.NewToolError(tr)
    assert te.Type() == "tool_error"
    assert te.Attr("ok") == starlark.False
    assert te.Attr("is_error") == starlark.True
    assert te.Attr("error").(starlark.String) == tr.Error
    assert te.Attr("detail").(starlark.String) == tr.Detail

criteria.action: allow dictionary key indexing on ToolError instances for keys 'error', 'detail', 'ok', and 'is_error'
criteria.contract: indexing e['error'], e['detail'], e['ok'], and e['is_error'] returns the respective values

setup: a ToolError instance returned to a Starlark script

criteria.condition: the built-in helper is_error(val) is evaluated
criteria.action: return True if val is a ToolError instance, and False for all other Starlark values
criteria.contract: is_error returns True for ToolError instances; is_error returns False for dicts, strings, integers, and None

setup: a Starlark script evaluating is_error with ToolError and non-error values

requirements.title: Concurrent execution helper (parallel)
requirements.rationale: Providing parallel dispatch helper functions enables scripts to execute batches of independent tool calls concurrently up to a configurable concurrency limit.

criteria.condition: call(tool_fn, **kwargs) is executed in a script
criteria.action: return a call descriptor capturing the target tool callable and keyword arguments
criteria.contract: returns a call descriptor capturing target tool callable and keyword arguments

setup: a Starlark script invoking call(target_tool, key='val', num=10)

criteria.condition: parallel(calls) is invoked with a list or tuple of call descriptors, tuples, or dicts
criteria.action: validate all call specifications, chunk them into batches of at most opts.MaxConcurrentCalls, and dispatch each batch via core.CallNested concurrently
criteria.contract: validates all calls against bound tools and remaining MaxCalls budget; chunks calls into concurrent batches of at most opts.MaxConcurrentCalls; dispatches each batch via core.CallNested concurrently

setup: options with MaxConcurrentCalls=2 and 5 call specifications (descriptors, tuples, dicts)
check.pseudocode:
calls := "parallel([call(work, i=1), (work, {'i': 2}), {'tool': work, 'args': {'i': 3}}, call(work, i=4), call(work, i=5)])"
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, calls, Options{MaxConcurrentCalls: 2})
assert res.OK
assert len(res.Data["return_value"].([]any)) == 5
assert maxConcurrentSeen <= 2

criteria.condition: concurrent batch calls complete across all workers
criteria.action: assemble the converted Starlark result values into a list matching the exact original order of the input calls
criteria.contract: results are assembled into a list matching the exact original order of the input calls

setup: tool calls with varying execution latencies executed via parallel
check.pseudocode:
script := "def main():\n return parallel([call(delayed, delay=50, id=1), call(delayed, delay=10, id=2), call(delayed, delay=30, id=3)])"
res := runScript(ctx, script)
assert res.OK
assert res.Data["return_value"] == []any{map[string]any{"id": 1}, map[string]any{"id": 2}, map[string]any{"id": 3}}

criteria.condition: any nested call within parallel triggers an interceptor termination returning core.ErrTerminated
criteria.action: immediately halt parallel batch execution and return with ToolResult.Terminate set to true
criteria.contract: parallel stops remaining calls and sets Terminate: true on the code-mode result

setup: a batch of parallel calls where one call encounters an interceptor terminate vote
check.pseudocode:
script := "parallel([call(normal_tool), call(terminating_tool), call(normal_tool)])"
res := runScript(ctx, script)
assert res.Terminate == true

requirements.title: Resource limits and budget enforcement
requirements.rationale: Enforcing timeouts, step limits, call counts, and output byte limits prevents runaway scripts from consuming excessive compute, memory, or context budget.

criteria.condition: script wall-clock execution time exceeds opts.MaxTimeout
criteria.action: halt execution cleanly and return a failure result identifying the timeout
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'timeout', and Detail indicating the elapsed timeout limit

setup: options configured with MaxTimeout=50ms and a long-running script
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "while True: pass", Options{MaxTimeout: 50 * time.Millisecond})
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "timeout"
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "50ms")

criteria.condition: script execution step count exceeds opts.MaxSteps configured on the Starlark thread
criteria.action: terminate script execution and return a step limit error
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'step_limit_exceeded', and Detail naming the step limit

setup: options configured with MaxSteps=100 and a script with an intensive loop
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "for x in range(1000): pass", Options{MaxSteps: 100})
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "step_limit_exceeded"
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "100")

criteria.condition: cumulative nested tool calls dispatched across direct calls and parallel exceed opts.MaxCalls
criteria.action: reject the excess call, halt script execution, and return a call limit error
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'call_limit_exceeded', and Detail naming the call limit

setup: options configured with MaxCalls=3
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "for i in range(5): ping()", Options{MaxCalls: 3})
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "call_limit_exceeded"
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "3")

criteria.condition: cumulative printed and returned output bytes exceed opts.MaxOutputBytes
criteria.action: halt script execution and return an output limit error
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'output_limit_exceeded', and Detail naming the output byte limit

setup: options configured with MaxOutputBytes=200 and a script generating extensive output
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "print('A' * 300)", Options{MaxOutputBytes: 200})
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "output_limit_exceeded"
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "200")

criteria.condition: script execution terminates due to any exceeded limit and partial printed output or completed nested calls exist
criteria.action: include the partial output and completed calls ledger in ToolResult.Data and format them in ToolResult.Text
criteria.contract: partial printed output and completed calls ledger are included in ToolResult.Data; partial output and completed calls summary are formatted in ToolResult.Text

setup: a script that prints output and performs tool calls before breaching a limit
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "print('step 1 completed'); ping(); print('A'*500)", Options{MaxOutputBytes: 100})
assert !res.OK
assert strings.Contains(res.Data["partial_output"].(string), "step 1 completed")
assert len(res.Data["calls_completed"].([]any)) == 1
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "step 1 completed")
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "ping")

requirements.title: Output capture, middle truncation, and disk spilling
requirements.rationale: Buffering printed output and script return values with middle truncation and spill file support prevents context blowup while preserving key beginnings and conclusions.

criteria.condition: a script calls the print built-in function
criteria.action: capture the formatted printed line into an internal tools.Accumulator configured with TruncateMiddle and capacity opts.MaxOutputBytes
criteria.contract: printed lines are captured into internal tools.Accumulator configured with TruncateMiddle and capacity opts.MaxOutputBytes

setup: a script executing multiple print calls
check.pseudocode:
res := runScript(ctx, "print('line 1'); print('line 2')")
assert res.OK
assert res.Text == "line 1\nline 2"

criteria.condition: script evaluation concludes successfully
criteria.action: determine the return value by executing main() if defined, else reading global variable result if defined, else defaulting to None
criteria.contract: executing main() takes precedence if defined; reading global variable result is used if main() is absent; defaults to None if neither is defined

setup: scripts defining main(), global variable result, or neither
check.pseudocode:
r1 := runScript(ctx, "def main(): return 'from_main'\nresult = 'from_result'")
assert r1.Data["return_value"] == "from_main"
r2 := runScript(ctx, "result = 'from_result'")
assert r2.Data["return_value"] == "from_result"
r3 := runScript(ctx, "x = 1")
assert r3.Data["return_value"] == nil

criteria.action: for any script execution, format ToolResult.Text with combined printed text and return value, printed text only, formatted return value only, or '[Script finished with no output]'
criteria.contract: both present: combines printed text and formatted return value; printed text only: returns printed text; return value only: returns formatted return value; neither present: returns '[Script finished with no output]'

setup: a generator of script execution outputs with varied printed text and return value states

criteria.condition: total output bytes exceed opts.MaxOutputBytes and opts.DisableSpill is false
criteria.action: truncate output via middle elision marker and stream full output to a spill file in opts.SpillDir
criteria.contract: output is truncated retaining head and tail with middle elision marker; full output is written to a spill file in opts.SpillDir; SpillPath points to valid on-disk file containing complete output

setup: options with MaxOutputBytes=200, SpillDir configured, and DisableSpill=false
check.pseudocode:
spillDir := t.TempDir()
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "print('HEAD' + 'X'*500 + 'TAIL')", Options{MaxOutputBytes: 100, SpillDir: spillDir, DisableSpill: false})
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "HEAD")
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "TAIL")
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "bytes elided")
assert res.Metadata.SpillPath != ""
data, _ := os.ReadFile(res.Metadata.SpillPath)
assert len(data) > 500

criteria.condition: total output bytes exceed opts.MaxOutputBytes and opts.DisableSpill is true
criteria.action: truncate output via middle elision marker without writing a spill file to disk
criteria.contract: output is truncated via middle elision marker; no spill file is written to disk and SpillPath is empty

setup: options with MaxOutputBytes=100 and DisableSpill=true
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "print('HEAD' + 'Y'*500 + 'TAIL')", Options{MaxOutputBytes: 100, DisableSpill: true})
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "bytes elided")
assert res.Metadata.SpillPath == ""

criteria.condition: output truncation occurs during script execution
criteria.action: populate core.ToolMetadata on ToolResult with Truncated: true, TruncatedBy: 'bytes', TotalBytes, SpillPath, and DurationMS
criteria.contract: populates core.ToolMetadata with Truncated: true and TruncatedBy: 'bytes'; populates TotalBytes, SpillPath, and DurationMS

setup: a script execution triggering output truncation
check.pseudocode:
res := runScriptWithOpts(ctx, "print('Z'*400)", Options{MaxOutputBytes: 100})
assert res.Metadata.Truncated == true
assert res.Metadata.TruncatedBy == "bytes"
assert res.Metadata.TotalBytes >= 400
assert res.Metadata.DurationMS >= 0

requirements.title: Script error diagnostics and telemetry ledger
requirements.rationale: Recording structured diagnostics and an execution ledger of completed calls ensures transparency for failures without rolling back side effects.

criteria.condition: a script encounters a syntax error during parsing
criteria.action: terminate execution and return a syntax error result detailing the file and line number
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'syntax_error', line number, and error details

setup: a script containing invalid Starlark syntax (e.g. unclosed parenthesis)
check.pseudocode:
res := runScript(ctx, "def foo(\n  return 1")
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "syntax_error"
assert res.Data["line"].(int) > 0
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "syntax")

criteria.condition: a script encounters a runtime execution error such as undefined variable or type mismatch
criteria.action: terminate execution and return a runtime error result with stack and line information
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'runtime_error', line number, and error details

setup: a script with a runtime error (e.g. division by zero or undefined variable access)
check.pseudocode:
res := runScript(ctx, "x = 1 / 0")
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "runtime_error"
assert res.Data["line"].(int) > 0
assert strings.Contains(res.Detail, "zero")

criteria.action: for any nested tool call executed during script run, append a record containing tool name, arguments, ok status, and error code to an execution ledger
criteria.contract: ledger records tool name, arguments, ok status, and error code for every nested call; records are ordered by chronological dispatch order

setup: a generator of scripts executing varied success and failure tool calls
check.pseudocode:
for script in gen_tool_call_scripts():
    res := runScript(ctx, script)
    ledger := res.Data["calls_completed"].([]any)
    for entry in ledger:
        m := entry.(map[string]any)
        assert m["tool"] != ""
        assert m["arguments"] != nil
        assert m["ok"] != nil

criteria.condition: a script execution completes, fails, or is halted by a limit
criteria.action: populate calls_completed in ToolResult.Data with the execution ledger and include the summary in ToolResult.Text without rolling back side effects
criteria.contract: calls_completed in ToolResult.Data contains the full execution ledger; ToolResult.Text formats the completed calls summary; tool side effects are not rolled back

setup: a script performing multiple tool calls and then failing at a subsequent step
check.pseudocode:
res := runScript(ctx, "ping(id=1); ping(id=2); fail_now()")
assert !res.OK
calls := res.Data["calls_completed"].([]any)
assert len(calls) == 2
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "ping(id=1)")
assert strings.Contains(res.Text, "ping(id=2)")

criteria.condition: the caller context is cancelled before or during script execution
criteria.action: halt execution cleanly and return an aborted result
criteria.contract: returns ToolResult with OK: false, Error: 'aborted', and Detail: 'Operation aborted'

setup: a caller context cancelled prior to or during script execution
check.pseudocode:
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
cancel()
res := runScript(ctx, "for i in range(1000): pass")
assert !res.OK
assert res.Error == "aborted"
assert res.Detail == "Operation aborted"

requirements.title: Offline example and documentation governance
requirements.rationale: Providing an offline end-to-end example and updated documentation validates code mode without external network dependencies and maintains architectural records.

criteria.action: provide an offline runnable example in examples/codemode/main.go binding navigation tools and an in-memory MCP tool against provider/faux without network access or API keys
provide an accompanying README in examples/codemode/README.md explaining how to run and verify the offline code-mode workflow
record the dependency adoption ruling for go.starlark.net in docs/DEPS.md documenting sandboxing, step budgeting, and pure-Go rationale
criteria.contract: default options match documented architecture (MaxTimeout 30s, MaxSteps 100k, MaxCalls 50, MaxConcurrentCalls 8, MaxOutputBytes 100KB); runtime provides deterministic execution without ambient host I/O

assert opts.MaxSteps == 100000
assert opts.MaxCalls == 50

execution_paths.title: Model executes a multi-step navigation and filtering script in code mode

steps.action: emits a tool call to 'code_mode' with a Starlark script that calls list_files and filters results
initializes a sandboxed Starlark thread and binds list_files as a keyword-argument function
invokes list_files(path='.') via core.CallNested and receives structured directory entries
filters the entries in Starlark and prints the filtered result list
captures printed output, formats ToolResult with the filtered list and completed calls ledger, and returns it to the agent loop

setup: a code-mode tool binding real navigation tool list_files and a test workspace directory
end_state: Starlark filters directory entries in memory
